steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hajj is the fifth Pillar of Islam — every Muslim who is physically and financially able must make the pilgrimage to Makkah at least once in their lifetime. Over 2 million Muslims perform Hajj each year during the month of Dhul-Hijjah.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Hajj: Pilgrimage
steps.body: 1. For Hajj: Pilgrimage questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Hajj: Pilgrimage to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: Approximately 25,000 British Muslims perform Hajj each year, according to the Council of British Hajjis. The British government works with Saudi authorities to facilitate the pilgrimage, and the UK Hajj Advisory Group provides guidance on travel, health and safety for British pilgrims.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: Malcolm X’s experience of Hajj in 1964 transformed his views on race. Writing from Makkah, he described seeing “blonde-haired, blued-eyed white-skinned Muslims” praying alongside Black Africans and Asians, all equal in ihram. This experience led him to reject the racial separatism of the Nation of Islam and embrace orthodox Sunni Islam’s message of universal brotherhood.

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
